messages:
Alex Nguyen: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — getting paged for elevated inference tail latency (p99 ~ 1.6s, baseline 600ms) across streaming and normal gen paths. Seeing a spike starting ~15:12 UTC. Root cause looks correlated to control-plane configfetch/auth errors. Posting traces/logs below, tagging @Riley for primary oncall handoff.

Riley Johnson: On it. Joining. Can you paste the top errors and affected regions/customers? I saw the alert for streaming stalls in US-EAST. @Molly can you check dashboards? 

Molly Chen: Looking at console: p95 jumped to ~450ms, p99 to ~1600ms for inference gateway. Streaming stalls reported by downstream telemetry (consumer ACK timeouts). Traces show long waits on configfetch RPCs and intermittent 429 from auth-token-store. Sample logs:

```
2026-03-15T15:12:07Z gateway | req_id=abc123 wait_for_config_ms=1203 upstream_error=503 config_fetch_error="timeout"
2026-03-15T15:12:09Z controlplane | req_id=abc124 feature_eval_wait_ms=980 db_err=too_many_requests token_store=429
```

Also seeing feature flag check latencies spiking (~800-1200ms) which correlates with KV fetch to configstore.

Jordan Patel: I can confirm ratelimiting traces between controlplane <-> configstore. There's burst tryCount increases. Hash: cff-keys hotkey fanout from many new connections this window.

Priya Rao: Customer impact — early look at logs shows degraded streaming responsiveness for ~4% of requests in the last 10m. Top 3 impacted tenants: acme-inc, prod-ecom, chatly-prod. SLOs: we breached p99 target for ~8 minutes so far. Need mitigation ASAP.

IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-20260315-1755559999. Severity: Sev2. Paging: oncall.eng-sre. Playbook: controlplane-backpressure. 

Riley Johnson: Steps I'm taking — 1) Fail open feature flag checks to avoid real-time evals; 2) Toggle configfetch fallback to cached-version; 3) Throttle/queue new configfetch requests at proxy layer to protect token-store. Will coordinate with infra to bump token-store RPS if needed.

Molly Chen: I can flip the fallback. Command to set cached fallback (run from ops-console):

```
# ops-console
POST /config/fallback
{ "mode": "use_cached", "ttl_s": 300 }
```

Doing it now. 

Alex Nguyen: After enabling fallback, streaming tail p99 reduced from 1.6s -> 820ms within ~90s. Good sign. But we still have elevated errors from auth tokenstore (429), which suggests injection of hotkeys or sudden fanout.

Jordan Patel: Recommend enabling short-circuit for feature flag paths for all inference-critical routes: route -> use static config until healthy. I can push a canary config to 5% first.

Riley Johnson: Can you prepare canary? I'll do a broader fallback if canary is green in 2min. Also request infra to check token-store CPU and DB pool availability.

Priya Rao: Customer comms draft: "We are investigating increased latency affecting streaming sessions and inference tail latency. Our mitigation is in progress; we will provide updates every 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:

Molly Chen: Approve. Also adding note: "If you see 503/stream stalls, reconnecting should resume session; we are throttling control-plane fetches to stabilize service." 

Jordan Patel: Canary rolled to 5% at 15:17 UTC. Telemetry shows immediate drop for that cohort. No increased errors.

Riley Johnson: Rolling fallback to 50% -> 100% now. Pushing policy: `configfetch.short_circuit = true` for inference routes.

```
# rollout snippet
deploy config-policy --target inference --short-circuit true --rollout 100
```

Alex Nguyen: After full rollout, overall p99 down to 540ms, p95 ~380ms. Streaming stalls decreased to baseline. IncidentBot alert: SLO breach cleared for p95 but p99 still borderline for a minute.

Molly Chen: Observed token-store queue length still elevated; infra reports token-store experiencing spike in token issuance (auth rate) likely from a misconfigured client retry loop. We should investigate the origin of burst.

Jordan Patel: I traced a fanout from an internal canary job that started at 15:10 UTC and had aggressive retry backoff bug. Open PR reference: git/infra/canary/retry-fix #412. That explains hotkey fanout and KV hotspot.

Riley Johnson: Good find. Mitigation steps: 1) Kill the runaway canary job (done) 2) Keep configfetch short-circuit for 10m 3) Ramp token-store RPS limit increased by infra to smooth backlog 4) Postmortem and alert threshold adjustments for hotkey fanout.

Alex Nguyen: I killed canary and confirmed no new hot fanout. Token-store RPS increased to +30% by infra. Queue draining in progress.

Priya Rao: Customer impact update: affected window ~15:10-15:25 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~120k across three tenants. We hit p99 SLO for ~8 minutes; we should offer credits per SLA if final postmortem shows impact >5min. 

Molly Chen: Monitoring: by 15:28 UTC p99 stabilized at 510ms, streaming ACK timeouts back to normal. Marking status: mitigated and monitoring.

Riley Johnson: Oncall handoff: I'm staying on for another 30m to ensure no regression, then will hand to next oncall (Jordan). Follow-ups: create incident ticket INC-20260315-1755559999 with actions:
- root cause: canary job retry bug -> token-store hotkey fanout -> configstore/backpressure -> inference tail latency
- mitigations performed: short-circuit configfetch, killed canary, increased token-store RPS
- customers impacted: acme-inc, prod-ecom, chatly-prod
- follow-ups: add rate-limit guard on canary jobs; alert for token-store queue length; improve fallback autopilot for featureflags

Jordan Patel: I'll take the 30m watch after Riley. I'll also open the follow-up PRs and schedule a postmortem for tomorrow. Assigning owners: Jordan -> infra guardrail PR, Molly -> monitoring alert tuning, Priya -> customer comms follow-up.

Alex Nguyen: Thanks team. Final note: add an automatic fallback to cached config for any fetch latency > 400ms to reduce blast radius next time. Also add a runbook subsection to check for internal canaries when token-store 429s spike.

Molly Chen: Adding runbook entries now. Marking thread status: resolved->monitoring. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident INC-20260315-1755559999 moved to status: MONITORING. Next update scheduled in 30m.
